reproduction_target: Cell-type-resolved genomic characterisation of Drosophila upd-tumour testis GSC-like and CySC-like cells. Computational target: (i) scRNA-seq processing and differential expression - Cell Ranger v7.0.0 (default parameters) -> Seurat SCTransform integrated assay with UMAP/clustering -> DecontX UMI decontamination -> shifted-logarithm normalisation -> pseudobulk log10 CPM via a limma linear model after compatible-isoform selection -> apeglm Bayesian posterior L2FC with covariates 'DecontX contamination score crossed with cell type' -> DEG selection (s-value < 1e-4, L2FC >= 1.5) and GO enrichment; (ii) ChIC-ChIP-seq (H3K4me3/H3K27me3/H3K9me3) processing - alignment to FlyBase D. melanogaster release 6.47 (Bowtie2 index per repo README) -> samtools view to data frame with Apache Beam fragment-midpoint computation -> MAPQ>=20 unique-mapping and paired-end fragment-length filtering -> 20 bp sliding-window midpoint binning -> maximum-likelihood Negative Binomial regression (H3 intercept + ChIC-ChIP L2FC) -> Gaussian-kernel (sigma = 40 bp) F-Seq-style smoothing and IP-over-H3-input log-fold BigWig tracks; (iii) Repli-seq four-fraction replication timing - 1 kb non-overlapping midpoint binning -> Bayesian logistic/Dirichlet-Multinomial regression over 3 kb windows (3 bins x 6 or 8 samples) giving a posterior expected logit timing score -> likelihood-ratio testing by numerical integration of full and reduced model likelihoods summarised as a Bayes factor, with pairwise cell-type calls in regions of width >= 20 kb -> LOESS smoothing, Z-scoring across cell types and mean-Z chromosomal-region summaries; plus the supplemental steps (pericentromeric heterochromatin epigenomic borders, rDNA auxiliary-sequence trimming, transposon-set regression) and the Imaris-based immunofluorescence quantification of Orc1/MCM2/Caf-p105-GFP. Wet-lab (fly genetics, immunostaining, 10x library prep, ChIC-ChIP bench protocol, Repli-seq BrdU/FACS/library prep) is out of scope.
granularity_note: Coarse step list built from the METHODS 'Bioinformatics', 'Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis', 'ChIC-ChIP sequencing analysis' and 'Replication sequencing analysis' subsections of the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML, one step per named tool or named analysis invocation. Where the paper prose omits a tool name that the linked repository README makes explicit (Bowtie2, samtools, Apache Beam, targets build system), the step is still enumerated from the prose analysis it performs and the README naming is recorded in the label; no workflow source was read line-by-line (that is Stage 2). Immunofluorescence quantification (Imaris + Mann-Whitney U) is counted as a C-layer step because Methods names the tool and the test and the result is a published statistic; the microscopy acquisition itself is counted in W.

steps.label: Wet-lab: fly husbandry and genetics - switchable dual-tagged histone cassette strains crossed into a UAS-upd background (Bloomington molasses food, 25 C); males aged ~2 days post-eclosion for genomics, 1-5 days for immunostaining; full stock list in Supplemental Material
Wet-lab: whole-mount and squash immunostaining of wild-type and upd-tumour testes, Hoechst counterstain, confocal imaging (antibody list in Supplemental Materials)

Wet-lab: testis dissociation (TrypLE Express + collagenase), 10x Genomics Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 3' Kit v3.1 library prep, pooled to 4 nM, Illumina NovaSeq S1 sequencing at the Johns Hopkins Genomics Core

Wet-lab: cell-specific sequential ChIC-ChIP (ProteinA-MNase-antibody directed cleavage in H3-GFP-expressing cells, bead capture, low/high-salt washes, crosslink reversal), NEBNext Ultra II DNA library prep, Illumina NovaSeq sequencing

Wet-lab: Repli-seq - BrdU incorporation, nuclei isolation, flow-sorting of GFP-positive nuclei into four S-phase fractions (early, early-mid, late-mid, late), ~10,000 nuclei per fraction, sonication, NEBNext Ultra II library prep, sequential anti-BrdU / anti-mouse IgG immunoprecipitation, NovaSeq sequencing
Reference ingestion and aligner index build: FlyBase D. melanogaster genome release 6.47 FASTA/feature files, Bowtie2 index (repo README maps this to R/targets-flybase.R)

Read alignment and fragment-midpoint pileup: Bowtie2 alignment, samtools view to data frame, Apache Beam column of fragment midpoints (prose says only 'alignment to FlyBase release 6.47'; tool names come from the repo README R/targets-zpileup.R and R/pileup.R)
scRNA-seq alignment and UMI quantification with Cell Ranger v7.0.0, default parameters

Dimension reduction and clustering: Seurat SCTransform integrated assay, UMAP embedding, cluster identification (repo R/sce.R, R/targets-sce.R; Seurat 5.0.3 / SeuratObject 5.0.1 / glmGamPoi 1.14.3 pinned in README REQUIREMENTS)
Ambient-RNA decontamination with DecontX (decontX 1.0.0) and shifted-logarithm normalisation of the DecontX-corrected counts
Pseudobulk log10 CPM after compatible-isoform selection and re-application of DecontX, fitted with a linear model (limma 3.56.2; repo R/targets-quantification.R, R/sce-quantification.R)
Posterior log-fold-change shrinkage by Bayesian regression coefficient estimation (apeglm 1.24.0; repo R/sce-deg.R) with covariates 'DecontX contamination score crossed with cell type'
DEG selection (s-value < 1e-4 and log effect size L2FC >= 1.5) and downstream Gene Ontology term enrichment
ChIC-seq read filtering and binning: uniquely-mapped reads only (MAPQ >= 20), paired-end fragment-length filtering, midpoint-only binning into 20 bp sliding genomic windows (repo R/targets-chic.R)

Maximum-likelihood Negative Binomial regression of nucleosome occupancy and ChIC-ChIP enrichment (intercept = H3 abundance, L2FC = ChIC-ChIP treatment) at 20 bp step (repo R/chic-enrichment.R; glmGamPoi 1.14.3)

Track generation: feature-density estimation from regression predictions smoothed with a Gaussian kernel sigma = 40 bp (F-Seq implementation, repo R/smooth-tile-track.R), log-fold enrichment of the IP track over the H3 input track, BigWig output (rtracklayer 1.62.0; repo R/chic-tracks.R)

Repli-seq binning: midpoints of single-end 100 bp reads or of properly paired alignments (up to 500 bp wide) binned into 1 kb non-overlapping steps genome-wide, with an autocorrelation check that consecutive bins are statistically independent (repo R/targets-repli.R, R/granges-regression.R)

Replication-timing inference: Bayesian logistic (Dirichlet-Multinomial, logistic prior and link, Beta-parameterised responses per repo R/repli-beta.R and R/repli-logistic.R) regression over 3 kb windows using 3 bins x 6 or 8 samples, summarised by the posterior expected value of the logit timing score (extraDistr 1.10.0, mvtnorm 1.2-4)

Static-versus-dynamic replication testing: likelihood-ratio test with numerical integration of the full and reduced model likelihoods summarised as a Bayes factor (pracma 2.4.4); pairwise cell-type null rejection in regions of width at least 20 kb

Timing-track smoothing and summarisation: LOESS smoothing of Repli-seq timing estimates, Z-scoring of several cell types at every genomic location, mean Z-scores across chromosomal regions to call static choreography versus replication bias (repo R/repli-chic-heatmap.R)

Supplemental annotation steps named in 'Bioinformatics': application of epigenomic borders of the pericentromeric heterochromatin for chromosome-region summaries; trimming rDNA-adjacent noncoding DNA from the rDNA auxiliary sequence file; regression of ChIC-ChIP enrichment on the unique transposon sequence set

Immunofluorescence quantification: Imaris image analysis of GFP-tagged Orc1, MCM2 and Caf-p105 in whole-mounted wild-type GSCs and CySCs, GFP intensity normalised to Hoechst DNA content, log2-transformed, compared by Mann-Whitney U test

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 11/17 (65%) RI, 5/17 (29%) NI, 1/17 (6%) X. This paper sits in the upper band of the stage-1 distribution: data and code are both genuinely released. Data - GEO GSE291929 is quoted verbatim in DATA ACCESS, is public since 12 Sep 2025 and carries 46 GSM sample records covering raw and processed scRNA-seq, ChIC-ChIP-seq and Repli-seq, so the Data axis is 2 for every sequencing-derived step. Code - https://github.com/ringw/Upd-Germline-Genomics is public, is the actual targets-based analysis workspace rather than a stub (532 commits, last push 2025-07-24), and its README maps each named analysis to a specific R file (targets-flybase.R, targets-zpileup.R/pileup.R, targets-chic.R, targets-quantification.R, targets-repli.R, targets-sce.R plus the helper functions), so the Code axis is 2 for the fourteen steps the workspace covers. The binding constraint on every step is Version, which is capped at 1 by construction at stage 1 and would stay at 1 even after a stage-2 check: the environment declaration is README 'Requirements' plus REQUIREMENTS.txt, which pin Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS, R 4.3.3 and twenty R packages with exact versions and install sources (e.g. apeglm 1.24.0 Bioconductor tar.gz, Seurat 5.0.3 CRAN tar.gz, Matrix 1.6-3 from the ubuntu focal-cran40 archive), but there is no renv.lock, no conda/mamba environment file, no Dockerfile or image digest, no tagged release and no Zenodo DOI - and the pinned list omits every non-R tool actually in the pipeline (Bowtie2, samtools, Apache Beam) as well as Cell Ranger. That omission is what pushes six steps below RI: C1 and C2 (Bowtie2/samtools/Beam, no version anywhere), C8 (the GO enrichment tool and ontology release are never named), C15 (LOESS span and degree unstated), C16 (the heterochromatin-border, rDNA-auxiliary and transposon-set input files have no accession, URL or version), and C17 (Imaris is proprietary, the microscopy images are not deposited and no quantification script exists). Under a successful stage-2 code check the eleven RI steps could not exceed RI on Version grounds, so the R-star gain from promoting this paper is zero - which is exactly why the tightened gate excludes exact_pins_partial.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps enumerated from the METHODS 'Bioinformatics', 'Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis', 'ChIC-ChIP sequencing analysis' and 'Replication sequencing analysis' subsections plus the Imaris/Mann-Whitney quantification in 'Immunostaining and image quantification'. 5 coarse wet-lab steps counted in W and excluded from |S|. Computational coverage = 17/22 (77%).

gaps.where: C1, C2 (Bowtie2, samtools, Apache Beam), C3 vs the requirements list, C8 (GO enrichment), C16, C17 (Imaris)
gaps.missing: The environment declaration is R-only. README 'Requirements' and REQUIREMENTS.txt pin Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS, R 4.3.3 and twenty R packages with exact versions and install sources, but no version is given anywhere - paper or repo landing page - for the aligner (Bowtie2), samtools, Apache Beam, or Imaris. Cell Ranger is pinned in the paper ('Cell Ranger (v7.0.0) with default parameters') but does not appear in REQUIREMENTS.txt at all, so the declared environment does not describe the tool that produced the count matrices. The Gene Ontology enrichment in C8 names neither a package nor an ontology release ('yielding enriched Gene Ontology (GO) terms'). There is no sessionInfo(), no Bioconductor release number, and REQUIREMENTS.txt itself lists only five entries (R, apeglm, Cairo, Matrix, Seurat) while the README lists twenty, so the two declarations disagree about scope.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish one software table covering the whole stack, not just the R layer: Bowtie2, samtools and the Apache Beam runtime with exact versions and build flags, Cell Ranger v7.0.0 with its reference transcriptome build, the GO enrichment package plus the ontology and annotation release dates, and Imaris with its version. Reconcile REQUIREMENTS.txt with the README list, and ship sessionInfo() from the machine that produced the figures.

gaps.where: C4 (Seurat SCTransform / UMAP / clustering), C5 (DecontX), C13 (Bayesian logistic regression posterior)
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported anywhere in the paper. UMAP embedding and graph-based clustering, the DecontX EM-based decontamination (applied twice - once for UMI correction and again before pseudobulk aggregation), and the posterior estimation behind the logit timing score are all stochastic, and cluster identity and the contamination score are load-bearing: the contamination score is used as a regression covariate in C7, so seed-dependent variation propagates into the reported posterior L2FC values and hence into the DEG list.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seed set for each stochastic call (or state that set.seed is fixed inside the targets pipeline and give its value), and state whether the reported DEG list is stable across seeds; at minimum quote the tolerance within which the contamination score and cluster assignments are reproducible.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C16 - external reference resources
gaps.missing: The genome is pinned by release ('FlyBase's Drosophila melanogaster genome (release 6.47)') but only in prose; no download URL, no file name, no checksum, and no statement of which FASTA/annotation flavour was ingested. The three supplemental resources in the 'Bioinformatics' paragraph are worse: the 'epigenomic borders of the pericentromeric heterochromatin' are cited to a reference rather than to a coordinate file, the 'rDNA auxiliary sequence file' is named without a source or accession and is then trimmed by an unstated rule, and the 'unique transposon sequence set' has no source or version. Whether the repository fetches these with a pinned rule (class A) or reads them from a user-supplied local path (class B) cannot be decided from prose and is a stage-2 question; at stage 1 all env_capture_class values are 'n/a'.
gaps.how_to_close: Give the exact FlyBase download URLs and checksums for the release-6.47 FASTA and annotation, deposit the heterochromatin border BED, the trimmed rDNA auxiliary sequence and the unique-transposon set as versioned supplementary files with checksums, and make the pipeline fetch each of them by a pinned, versioned URL inside the workflow rather than from a local path.

gaps.where: C17 - Imaris quantification of Orc1-GFP, MCM2-GFP and Caf-p105-GFP
gaps.missing: The only quantification route for the replication-licensing-factor comparison between GSCs and CySCs is Imaris, a proprietary closed-source GUI application, used at an unstated version with unstated segmentation and surface-creation settings. No macro, batch script or exported settings file is deposited in the repository, whose contents are entirely genomic (R/, chic/, repli/, scRNA-seq/, transcriptome/). The underlying confocal image stacks are not in GEO and no image repository (IDR, BioImage Archive, Zenodo) is named.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw confocal stacks in an image archive with accessions, export and deposit the Imaris analysis settings (or reimplement the segmentation in an open tool such as Fiji/CellProfiler and deposit that script), and state the Imaris version, the segmentation parameters and the normalisation formula used for GFP-over-Hoechst.

gaps.where: Linkage between GEO GSE291929 (46 GSM records) and the repository's sample sheets (scRNA-seq-Metadata.csv, scRNA-seq-Assay-Metadata.csv, geoSubmission/)
gaps.missing: The paper states only 'All raw and processed sequencing data ... under the accession number GSE291929' and never maps a GSM or a FASTQ file name to a step, a cell type (GSC-like versus CySC-like), a histone mark, or an S-phase fraction (early / early-mid / late-mid / late). The repository README describes the entry point as 'a sample sheet (of SRA accessions, after publication)', which signals that the accession column in the committed metadata may be a placeholder pending publication rather than the live mapping. A third party therefore cannot tell which of the 46 samples feeds which of the four Repli-seq fractions or which ChIC-ChIP antibody arm without inspecting the repository files - a stage-2 check.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a sample-to-accession table in the paper's supplementary material mapping each GSM to cell type, assay, antibody or S-phase fraction and replicate, and make the repository sample sheet carry the final GSM/SRR identifiers rather than post-publication placeholders.

gaps.where: Repository entry point run.sh / run.R and the committed _targets/ store
gaps.missing: The documented way to run the analysis is 'nohup nice -4 R CMD BATCH run.R &' with a commented-out 'module load R # Uncomment if R is an environment module', i.e. the pipeline assumes an HPC-style module environment and a single declared platform (Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS) with no abstraction over it. A _targets/ store is committed at the repository root, so the build state travels with the code and may encode absolute paths from the authors' machine. No container, no conda environment and no Makefile-level entry point is provided as an alternative. Whether absolute paths are in fact hardcoded is a stage-2 question; at stage 1 only the entry-point shape and the declared single platform are on the record.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a container (or a conda/renv lock) so the analysis does not depend on a site-specific module system, parameterise all input and output roots through a config file, and either exclude the _targets/ store from version control or document that it is provided purely as a cache with paths relative to the repository root.

gaps.missing: The repository is public and substantive but entirely mutable: no tagged release, no GitHub release, no Zenodo DOI badge, no Software Heritage identifier, and no license file. The paper cites it as a bare URL with no commit hash and no access date, and the repository has been pushed to as recently as 2025-07-24 (after the v2 preprint). Nothing identifies the state of the code that produced the published figures, and the absence of a license leaves reuse rights unstated.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag the exact commit used for the published figures, archive that tag to Zenodo for a DOI, cite the DOI (or at least the commit hash) in DATA ACCESS instead of the bare repository URL, and add an explicit open-source license.

gaps.where: C15 (LOESS), C13/C14 (prior and Bayes-factor thresholds), C4 (SCTransform/UMAP/clustering settings)
gaps.missing: Several quantitative decisions are described qualitatively. LOESS smoothing is named with no span, degree or weighting. The Bayes factor is described as the summary of the numerical integration but no acceptance threshold is quoted, only the region-width criterion ('regions of width at least 20kb'). The Dirichlet-Multinomial model's prior hyperparameters are described only as 'Logistic prior and Logistic link function'. The Seurat path gives no number of principal components, no clustering resolution and no integration anchor settings. Each of these is recoverable in principle from the deposited R code, which is why the affected steps sit at NI or RI rather than X, but none is recoverable from the paper alone.
gaps.how_to_close: State the LOESS span and degree, the Bayes-factor cutoff used to call differential replication, the prior hyperparameters of the timing model, and the SCTransform/PCA/clustering settings in Methods, or point each Methods sentence at the specific repository file and function that fixes them.

gaps.missing: Fly husbandry and genetics, whole-mount and squash immunostaining, 10x library preparation, the sequential ChIC-ChIP bench protocol and the Repli-seq BrdU/FACS/library workflow are wet-lab and out of computational-reproduction scope. They are recorded because they gate the data: the detailed immunostaining protocol, the antibody list and the fly stock list are all deferred to 'Supplemental Material', and both the ChIC and the Repli-seq protocols are given in brief with the full procedure cited to prior publications.
gaps.how_to_close: No action required for computational reproducibility; for wet-lab replication, deposit the full ChIC-ChIP and Repli-seq protocols on protocols.io with DOIs and give RRIDs for the antibodies and fly stocks.
